title: Depression, Recovery, and Total War
partB: Hoover's preferred method against the Depression: voluntary cooperation by business, charity, and local government, without federal compulsion or direct relief.
The 1941 program by which the United States supplied Britain, and later the Soviet Union, with war materiel, abandoning neutrality in everything but name.
The drought and wind erosion that stripped the southern Plains' topsoil through the 1930s and drove farm families west.
Roosevelt's February 1942 order authorizing the military to remove Japanese Americans from the West Coast to internment camps.
Roosevelt's 1937 proposal to add a new justice for each sitting justice over seventy, aimed at a Court that had voided New Deal laws.
The Pacific strategy of seizing selected islands as stepping stones and bypassing Japanese strongholds on the road to Japan.
The electoral alliance of labor unions, big cities, farmers, the white South, and Black voters in the North that kept the Democratic Party dominant for a generation.
The emblem of the millions of women who took industrial war jobs between 1942 and 1945.
